text:
viv: Heads-up - Partner PrismLane submitted their June marketplace invoice PL-JUN and several customer lines show negative billed amounts (credits > charges). Looks like they applied a promotional credit twice for the same metered events. Anyone else seeing this?

arthur: I pulled their CSV vs our meter. For customer CL-221 the ledger looks like: reported_units=45,000, unit_price=0.05, gross=2250, credits_applied=2xPROMO-2026 -> net=-150. Their export apparently applied the promo both at export time and then again during their downstream billing conversion.

sophie: Example snippet from their CSV: 

```
customer_id,units,unit_price,gross,credits
CL-221,45000,0.05,2250,PROMO-2026;PROMO-2026
CL-330,8000,0.05,400,PROMO-2026
CL-887,12000,0.05,600,
```

partner-finance: We replicated this locally. Our billing team had a two-stage workflow: marketing applied promo flags in the sales export and the billing export also applied promo logic because a feature flag was on for legacy partners. The result is duplicate credit application for ~12 customers. We've paused downstream invoice posting and are preparing corrected invoices + credit reversals for the negatives. ETA 4 business days.

viv: Given month close tomorrow, how do we handle accounting? We have negative invoice totals that would reduce revenue incorrectly if posted as-is. Recommendation?

arthur: We should not recognize negative net invoices as final until partner corrects. For customers where net < 0 we should treat the absolute value as a receivable to be refunded to end-customer and not reduce our recognized revenue for marketplace take. My proposal: post provisional reclassification entries moving the negative amount from "partner settlements" to "customer refund liability" GL 2-410 and block recognition until corrected artifacts arrive.

sophie: Agreed. Also create a contingency JV that zeros out the negative revenue impact on our revenue GL (4-160 "Marketplace Partner Credits") and hold a corresponding liability. Once partner issues corrected invoices we reverse the JV and process refunds or net settlements.

partner-finance: PrismLane also offered to issue a one-line consolidated corrected invoice and a confirmation they will absorb any customer refunds if we elect to have them net the refunds. They requested we wait for their corrected artifacts.

viv: OK let's proceed with provisional JVs to avoid misstatement. Can billing team create JV(s) per customer group? Keep amounts granular for audit. Also tag with reason_code "partner_double_credit".

billing-bot: Provisional JVs created: JV-2026-0899 (group A: JV lines for customers CL-221, CL-330; total $2,400) and JV-2026-0900 (group B: remaining affected customers; total $1,150). GL 2-410 status: PENDING_VENDOR_CONFIRMATION. Tickets FIN-4825 and FIN-4826 opened.

arthur: I'll add a note to month-close pack explaining the treatment and linking FIN-4825/4826. Also adding a recommendation to add a pre-ingest guardrail: disallow applying the same promo ID more than once per customer per billing period. I'll open INFRA-7902.

sophie: I'll draft the partner-facing message (for record):

"Subject: PL-JUN - duplicate promo credits detected

Hi PrismLane billing team,

Thanks for the update. We've temporarily blocked posting of PL-JUN and posted provisional JVs (JV-2026-0899 / JV-2026-0900) to avoid revenue misstatement and to capture potential customer refunds. Please send corrected invoice(s) and a note confirming whether PrismLane will absorb refunds or net settle within 4 business days to billing@redwood.ai. Once we receive corrected artifacts we'll reverse the provisional entries and reconcile.

Best,
Sophie (Finance)"

partner-finance: We'll push PrismLane to expedite. Also providing an RCA template showing both the marketing flag and the legacy billing conversion steps so your auditors have it.

viv: Leave this thread open until corrected invoices or confirmations are attached to FIN-4825/4826. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
